name: transfer-funds-card

frames.best_why: Whole card at rest with every field, the summary and the confirm button visible and nothing covered.

tagline: Money transfer sheet with an amount, two account rows and a fee summary.
summary: A compact transfer form: an amount, From and To account rows with dropdown chevrons, a three-line summary of arrival, fee and total, and one confirm button. Rows and the button respond to hover.
appearance: A dark rounded card with a title, a close cross and a short description. Three grey pill rows hold the amount and two account numbers with paired chevrons, a bordered summary lists arrival, fee and total, and a white pill button sits at the bottom.
behaviour: Hovering an account row wobbles its chevrons and deepens the row's shade; the close cross turns and the confirm button springs slightly larger, shrinking on press. Otherwise the card is a still form with values already filled in.
demo_content: A $2,450.00 transfer from Everyday Checking (··8402) to Emergency Savings (··1192), arriving today.
search_phrases: amount with from and to accounts
send money between my own accounts
use_when: A banking app needs one self-contained step for moving money between a person's own accounts.
avoid_when: It is display only: the account rows open nothing, so choosing a different account needs wiring outside the card.
customise: Title, description, amount, currency, both account strings, summary rows and the button label are props, plus confirm and close callbacks and a class override.
weight_why: A static form with a couple of hover springs; nothing animates until the pointer arrives.

a11y.note: Close and Confirm are real buttons, but the account rows are plain divs with no role, label or key handling.

issues: The account rows look like pickers but are plain divs, so clicking them does nothing.
All six frames look nearly identical, so the hover wiggle and spring are never captured.
polish_why: Clean spacing and a believable banking card; the account rows present as controls but are inert.
